0 - Generating a dummy SQL database - Universities data

George Melrose

2024-04-26

This RMD generates the dummy data to be worked with in this project.

1.Generating the 6 tables for the ‘University Rankings’ Dataset

“There are a few hundred universities in the sample data, and 21 different ranking criteria across three different systems. The data exists for the years 2005 to 2016.It doesn’t contain every world university, or data up until 2018 or 2019.”

I used sqlite code from this github to generate the fake database - https://github.com/bbrumm/databasestar/tree/main/sample_databases/sample_db_university/sqlite

country

This is a simple list of countries that were in the data set. Not a complete list of all countries, but enough for this excercise.

university

A list of universities that were ranked in this system. Each university is related to a country.

ranking_system

This contains the three different ranking systems used: Times Higher Education World University Ranking, Shanghai Ranking, and Center for World University Rankings.

ranking_criteria

This table contains the different criteria used in each ranking system, such as Citations and Quality of Education. It also contains criteria for the Total Score for each system.

university_year

The university_year table contains values for measurements such as the number of students and the student to staff ratio for each university in several years.

university_ranking_year

This table contains the score for each year for each university and ranking criteria. It’s the largest table in the database.

The ‘University Rankings’ data is explained here, with ERD below- https://www.databasestar.com/sample-database-university-rankings/

Remember, keys joined together need to be of the same data type!

knitr::include_graphics("C:/Users/gam55/Downloads/universities_erd.png")

  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  country_name TEXT DEFAULT NULL

Ranking System

CREATE TABLE ranking_system (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  system_name TEXT DEFAULT NULL
);
INSERT INTO ranking_system (id, system_name) VALUES
(1,'Times Higher Education World University Ranking'),
(2,'Shanghai Ranking'),
(3,'Center for World University Rankings');

Ranking Criteria

CREATE TABLE ranking_criteria (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  ranking_system_id INTEGER DEFAULT NULL,
  criteria_name TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
  CONSTRAINT fk_rc_rs FOREIGN KEY (ranking_system_id) REFERENCES ranking_system (id)
);

University

CREATE TABLE university (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  country_id INTEGER DEFAULT NULL,
  university_name TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
  CONSTRAINT fk_uni_cnt FOREIGN KEY (country_id) REFERENCES country (id)
)

University Year (Statistics about Universities per Year)

CREATE TABLE university_year (
  university_id INTEGER DEFAULT NULL,
  year INTEGER DEFAULT NULL,
  num_students INTEGER DEFAULT NULL,
  student_staff_ratio REAL DEFAULT NULL,
  pct_international_students INTEGER DEFAULT NULL,
  pct_female_students INTEGER DEFAULT NULL,
  CONSTRAINT fk_uy_uni FOREIGN KEY (university_id) REFERENCES university (id)
)
# List the tables present in the database connected through 'con'
tables <- dbListTables(con)

# Print the list of tables
print(tables)

University Ranking Year

  university_id INTEGER DEFAULT NULL,
  ranking_criteria_id INTEGER DEFAULT NULL,
  year INTEGER DEFAULT NULL,
  score INTEGER DEFAULT NULL,
  CONSTRAINT fk_ury_rc FOREIGN KEY (ranking_criteria_id) REFERENCES ranking_criteria (id),
  CONSTRAINT fk_ury_uni FOREIGN KEY (university_id) REFERENCES university (id)
)

print(tables)

Saving tables for future use

# Get a list of all tables in the connection
tables <- dbListTables(con)

# Loop through each table and write it to a CSV file
for (table in tables) {
  # Read the table from the SQL connection
  data <- dbReadTable(con, table)
  
  # Write the table to a CSV file
  write.csv(data, paste0(table, ".csv"), row.names = FALSE)
}
